primitives.name: Layout Composition Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: # app-layouts — the standard Higgsfield app layouts (`type: "app"` builds ONLY) A `type: "app"` product must look and feel like a Higgsfield product, so you do NOT invent app chrome.
primitives.assumptions: All applications must conform to predefined layout schemas; no ad-hoc UI elements allowed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When user requests non-standard layout, fallback to nearest canonical template.

layer2.mapping: Each layout corresponds to a unique topological embedding of UI components that preserves semantic relationships between input/output channels.
layer2.telemetry: Template adherence score based on component usage frequency and positional fidelity.

primitives.name: Code as Source of Truth
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Read the code, then build.** After `higgsfield website repo-access` + clone, read `app/src/layouts/AGENTS.md` (the layout catalog — anatomy + rules for each) AND `app/src/components/AGENTS.md` (the MANDATORY component contract, with copy-paste wiring), then open the layout/component files you'll use.
primitives.assumptions: Implementation correctness depends entirely on reading and applying existing code artifacts.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when developers rely on memory or external references instead of repository code.

layer2.mapping: Repository-based development enforces a derived kernel of reusable components and layout structures, enabling scalable and consistent application construction.
layer2.telemetry: Build success rate correlated with adherence to documented component contracts.

primitives.name: Template-Based Adaptation
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## The six layouts (`app/src/layouts/`) Copy the closest one into your route and adapt freely.
primitives.assumptions: Adaptation is bounded by the six canonical layout types; deviation requires justification.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Custom layouts are permitted only when none of the six templates adequately represent the desired functionality.

layer2.mapping: Each adapted layout maintains isomorphism with its parent template while allowing local modifications to suit specific use cases.
layer2.telemetry: Number of deviations from base template normalized against total customization scope.

The foundational principle of Higgsfield app design centers on the notion of compositional identity: all products must derive their visual and functional integrity from a shared set of layout kernels. This ensures that even as individual features evolve, the core UX remains invariant. The system operates under a dual constraint—first, that no new UI chrome may be invented, and second, that all construction proceeds from existing code. These constraints form a closed-loop feedback mechanism where the repository becomes both the generator and validator of design decisions. As such, the layout selection process is not merely heuristic but algorithmic, mapping user intent onto a finite set of canonical forms. Each template encodes a distinct operational logic: Studio for generative workflows, Preset for style-based creation, App Detail for marketing, AI Stylist for iterative refinement, Skin Enhancer for before/after comparisons, and Shots for stepwise generation. These templates are not just interfaces but computational abstractions that encode domain-specific behaviors. The enforcement of this structure prevents fragmentation and enables seamless integration across platforms. Any deviation from these templates must be justified by a clear mismatch with the available options—a condition that introduces a meta-level decision-making layer into the development workflow. Thus, the entire architecture can be viewed as a lattice of permissible transformations, where each node represents a valid instantiation of a layout kernel, and edges denote allowable adaptations. The mathematical rigor lies in maintaining this lattice structure while permitting controlled variation through parameterized components.
